newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian MPs start debate on land sales ban.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian MPs start debate on land sales ban.

text.p: Palestinian legislators began on Monday to debate a draft law banning the sale of land to Israelis after the killing last month of three Arab land brokers.

The Council's legal committee drafted the law after sharp criticism from the United States and Israel directed at the Palestinian Authority for activating a Jordanian military regulation which bans land sales to Israelis.
Last month's announcement of the ban was followed by the killing of three Arab land dealers by unidentified assailants.
The 11-point draft, presented to the 88 legislators in the West Bank city of Ramallah, is intended to protect Palestinian land and stop the expansion of Jewish settlements on Arab soil.
The draft law stated that Palestinians who sold land to Israelis would be committing a "great treason" and should be "given the maximum punishment stated in laws implemented in Palestine".
The phrasing was a reference to capital punishment, which is mentioned in the Jordanian law, but it stopped short of formally setting death as the maximum penalty.
All council members agreed that Palestinians selling land to Israelis should be punished, but they disagreed on the penalty.
Legislator Youssef al-Shanti criticised the draft law for not explicity stating that land brokers "should be hanged until dead".

But lawmaker Ziad Abu Amr said: "If the council decides that punishment will be capital punishment, I will be against it, but that doesn't mean the Palestinians shouldn't protect their land, this is a very legitimate issue."
The proposed legislation said that "non-Palestinian Arabs are banned from owning property in Palestine for any reason whatsoever with the exception of inheritance".

It said Arabs would be allowed to purchase Palestinian land through a special law issued by the Palestinian Authority. Foreign diplomats and investors, but not Israelis, would also be excluded from the ban.

Taking into consideration that many Palestinians hold dual nationality, the draft law stated they would be given a year to register their property with the Palestinian Authority "otherwise ownership of that property would be turned over to the Palestinian Authority".
In the case of Palestinians with foreign passports, the draft did set a penalty for land sales to Israelis -- life imprisonment with hard labour.
"Violators' property would be confiscated and turned over to the Palestinian Authority," it added.
The draft law stipulated no statute of limitations for land sales.
Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen said 20 Palestinians have been detained by the Authority for interrogation on suspicion of selling land to Israelis.
